quotes.why: The passage the paragraph introduces with རྣམ་བཤད་ལས — Gyaltsab Je's closing sentence on the six superknowledges, quoted almost word for word. Found by direct search.

quotes.text: མཐའ་དཔྱད་པ་ལ། མངོན་ཤེས་ཀྱི་རྟེན། བརྟེན་པ་མངོན་ཤེས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན། ས་མཚམས། རྒྱུ། དགོས་པ། ཁྱད་པར་དང་དྲུག་ལས།
quotes.why: The yig cha's own six-point division of the analysis of the superknowledges, which shows that the ལྔ་པ opening this paragraph is 'purpose' (དགོས་པ). Found by direct search.
The root-verse line on which this whole excursus hangs: the six 'qualities of superknowledge' as one of the ten instructions. Found by direct search.

Haribhadra's whole gloss on the six superknowledges: what each does, and that they are to be realised as primordially at peace. Nothing on their purpose, results or activities. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04020_THEG PA CHEN PO MDO SDE'I RGYAN ZHES BYA BA'I TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA (Mahāyana Sūtrālaṃkāra Nāma Kārikā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The first Sūtrālaṃkāra verse the paragraph cites, in the Tengyur's own text: the power's results, abiding, worship and purification.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04026_MDO SDE'I RGYAN GYI BSHAD PA (Sūtrālaṃkāra Vyākhyā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: Vasubandhu's gloss dividing the verse into three results, which is where the paragraph's མདོར་ན summary comes from.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 2 (BI)/TD04029_THEG PA CHEN PO'I MDO SDE'I RGYAN GYI RGYA CHER BSHAD PA (Mahāyāna Sūtrālaṃkāra Ṭīkā)_unicode.txt
quotes.text: འཕགས་པའི་གནས་པ་ནི་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་དང། མཚན་མ་མེད་པ་དང། སྨོན་པ་མེད་པ་དང། འཕགས་པའི་བདེན་པ་བཞི་དང། ས་དང་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པས་བསྡུས་པའོ། །ལྷའི་གནས་པ་ནི་བསམ་གཏན་དང་གཟུགས་མེད་པའོ། །ཚངས་པའི་གནས་ནི་བྱམས་པ་དང། སྙིང་རྗེ་དང། དགའ་བ་དང། བཏང་སྙོམས་སོ། །
quotes.why: The Indian sub-commentary's identification of the three abidings: wider than the yig cha's, taking in the four truths, the grounds and perfections, and the formless absorptions. Found by direct search.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04026_MDO SDE'I RGYAN GYI BSHAD PA (Sūtrālaṃkāra Vyākhyā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: Vasubandhu counts six activities in four verses. The yig cha counts three.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04026_MDO SDE'I RGYAN GYI BSHAD PA (Sūtrālaṃkāra Vyākhyā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: Vasubandhu reads the verse's ཆགས་དང་འཇིག as the formation and destruction of world-systems, against the yig cha's ཆགས་དང་འཇིགས.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04026_MDO SDE'I RGYAN GYI BSHAD PA (Sūtrālaṃkāra Vyākhyā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: Vasubandhu's three emanations (craft, birth, supreme), the reading behind the verse line the yig cha gives as ལས་དང་སྐྱེ་དང་ཞིང་མཆོག.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04026_MDO SDE'I RGYAN GYI BSHAD PA (Sūtrālaṃkāra Vyākhyā)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: Vasubandhu's three endowments, which the paragraph's closing གཞན་ཡང clause reproduces item for item.
Tsongkhapa's own fifth point on the superknowledges: their benefits, taken from Ārya Vimuktisena and not from the Sūtrālaṃkāra. Found by direct search.
Vimuktisena's list of the benefits of superknowledge, which Tsongkhapa, Jamyang Zhepa and Khedrup Tenpa Dargye follow. Found by direct search.
Jamyang Zhepa (Gomang) gives the same fifth point as the function of each superknowledge in turn, arranged by the two accumulations.

quotes.citation: Khedrup Tenpa Dargye, རྣམ་བཤད་སྙིང་པོ་རྒྱན་གྱི་སྣང་བ། (Sera Me spyi don), མངོན་ཤེས་དྲུག་གི་དགོས་པ།
quotes.why: The Sera Me textbook at the same fifth point: Vimuktisena's list of benefits, with only the last Sūtrālaṃkāra verse attached.

quotes.text: བཞི་པ་ནི། མངོན་པར་ཤེས་པ་དྲུག་པོ་ཆོས་ཅན། བྱེད་ལས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་དང་ལྡན་ཏེ། མཐོང་བ་དང་སྟོན་པའི་བྱེད་ལས། འོད་ཟེར་འགྱེད་པའི་བྱེད་ལས། རྣམ་པར་རོལ་བ་དང་སྤྲུལ་པའི་བྱེད་ལས། ཞིང་དག་པར་བྱེད་པའི་བྱེད་ལས་དང་ལྡན་པའི་ཕྱིར།
quotes.why: A later commentary that takes over the yig cha's wording but counts four activities, restoring Vasubandhu's 'display and emanation'.
Jamyang Shantipa assigns each clause of Gyaltsab's sentence to one superknowledge, which is the key to reading the first half of the paragraph.
The question that opens this section of the yig cha, naming the lemma and calling the six superknowledges the cause that completes every quality of practice. Found by direct search.
Panchen Sonam Drakpa's heading: the six superknowledges are the cause by which practice is quickly completed. This is Gyaltsab's claim made into a heading.
